items.stem: In big-O notation, what does O(n) say about an algorithm?

options.text: It always takes exactly n steps to finish
Its running time grows at most linearly with the input size
It uses n bytes of memory whatever the input
It is faster than every O(log n) algorithm

readingJson.reason: Big-O notation describes an asymptotic upper bound, so O(n) means the algorithm's running time grows no faster than a constant multiple of the input size n. Options A and C incorrectly imply exact values, and D is wrong because asymptotic bounds ignore constant factors and lower-order terms that determine actual speed for any given input.
